title: Contextual scope binding and immutable role attributes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement: Our current RBAC surface has grown organic and tightly coupled to tenant/organization boundaries. We need a v2 role model that enables: (1) deterministic permission evaluation with minimal runtime cost, (2) flexible, context-aware scoping (resource-level binds, not just tenant/global), (3) safe operations for enterprise admins (delegation, auditable elevation), and (4) SSO/SAML-friendly attribute mappings. This ticket proposes a model that treats roles as identities with immutable attribute keys and separately stores ephemeral scope bindings. Roles carry an immutable attribute set (role metadata) and a canonical permission template. Bindings connect roles to resource scopes with optional constraints (time, IP, purpose). The evaluation flow is: principal -> effective role bindings (including inherited scopes) -> permission template expansion -> constraint checks -> allow/deny. Key motivations: immutability of role attributes simplifies caching and reasoning (role templates do not change frequently), while bindings can be created/rotated without modifying the template. This separation enables safe rollouts, predictable caching (role template hash), and compact audit records (record binding_id + template_hash).
decisions: Adopt role-template + binding separation: role templates are immutable once created; updates create a new template version.
Store bindings as first-class objects: binding contains resource path, allowed actions, constraint predicates, created_by, expires_at.
Evaluation semantics: deny-overrides for explicit denies, otherwise allow-by-explicit-action; no wildcard implicit allows across unrelated resources.
Inheritance: resource hierarchy supports explicit 'cascade' flag on bindings; default is non-cascading to avoid accidental lateral privilege expansion.
Audit model: record binding_id, template_hash, evaluation_trace_id (UUID) for each authorization decision for downstream SLOs and forensic queries.
SSO/SAML: map federated attributes to role bindings via a configurable mapping layer; do not auto-create admin-capable bindings from SAML assertions without additional approval flow.

Emergency access (break-glass): implement time-limited elevated bindings with multi-step approval and an immediate audit marker; these bindings are flagged as "break_glass" and excluded from auto-remediation until closed.
Performance: cache expanded permission sets per (principal, template_hash) and invalidate on binding changes affecting the principal's resources.
Data model: Postgres primary store + Redis for hot permission caches; bindings indexed by resource path prefix for fast lookup.
Migration approach: support dual-mode for 3 months: legacy role checks route through adapter; new checks use binding/template model.
acceptance_criteria: API: /roles, /role_templates, /bindings endpoints implemented with CRUD and audit metadata.
Evaluation: authz library implements deterministic evaluation per RFC and unit tests for inheritance/cascade/deny semantics.
Performance: p95 authz decision < 4ms for cached principals; cold lookup < 15ms with indexed bindings for typical org sizes.
Audit: every auth decision logs evaluation_trace_id, binding_ids, template_hash, resolution path and is ingestible by existing logging pipeline.
SSO: SAML mapping UI prototype exists in console that allows mapping IdP attributes to role_templates and requires approval for admin-mapping.
Failover: if authz service is degraded, service should default to fail-closed for admin routes and fail-open for read-only non-sensitive product routes per policy.
Migration: provide a migration script and compatibility adapter; run on staging with replayed traffic and validate no permission regressions.
comments: 2025-01-16 — Ava Martinez: Drafted initial problem statement and proposed role-template separation. Linked design RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RBAC/RBAC+v2+Template+Binding+RFC

2025-01-22 — Ethan Cole: Early implementation notes: prototype stored templates as immutable rows with template_hash; bindings reference template_id. Experiment shows 12% reduction in cache churn compared to mutating templates.

2025-01-28 — Priya Desai (security review): Concern: SAML attribute mapping could be abused if IdP provides 'role' claim. Recommendation: require an explicit onboarding approval workflow and ZTA verification before auto-creating any binding that grants admin-like actions.

2025-01-30 — Design feedback (Liam O'Connor): Recommend clearer UX for 'cascade' vs 'scope' binding — users frequently conflate resource hierarchical scope with project-level membership. We'll prototype a hierarchical picker that visualizes cascade effects.

2025-02-03 — Implementation update (Ethan Cole): Implemented binding index on (resource_path_prefix, subject_id) and added Redis cache keyed by principal_id:template_hash. Benchmarks: cold lookup for 100k bindings took 9ms median on staging cpu. Pushing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/pull/4821

2025-02-05 — QA (Maya Lin): Added test cases for conflicting bindings (explicit deny on child resource vs allow on parent) — correct result: deny wins. Filing follow-up ENG-22789 for UI visualization of conflicting bindings.
2025-02-05 — Compliance (Jamal Brooks): Audit requirements confirmed: logs must be retained 2 years for enterprise tier. Need to add retention config to audit pipeline.
